about: The behavioural parity corpus for the bridge's VENDORED PHP copy of the coordination framework's Python terminal-column rule (card#10273, adopting the primitive card#9936 / DL-414 built). The bridge cannot import Python, so it re-implements the rule; this file is the contract between the two copies, and it is RUNNABLE at both ends. Every entry is an ARGUMENT -> ANSWER pair, never a text comparison: the two ends are different languages, so a textual diff of them is undefined.

authority.relationship: The coordination framework OWNS this rule. The bridge mirrors it, because `bridge:check`'s DL-200 cross-config compare has to answer 'what does the OTHER mover consider terminal' in PHP. A disagreement is the bridge's defect to fix by re-mirroring, never the framework's to fix by matching the bridge.

how_the_far_end_runs_this: Run this repo's `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py --corpus docs/coord-terminals-parity-corpus.json [--coord-examples <your templates/kanban/examples>]`. It binds the `coord` package to the directory named, so the scripts' own `from coord.kanban_common import …` resolves THERE and never to an installed copy elsewhere on `sys.path`; it refuses to measure (exit 2) if any `coord` function the scripts hold comes from a file outside that directory, and it prints the sha256 of every file it executed. It imports `kanban_common.terminals_for_board` and `kanban-inbox-check._terminal_columns_by_board` FROM SOURCE and executes every vector below against them — it never re-implements the rule (the board-id join and the placeholder skip ARE the rule under test, so a local copy of that loop would agree by construction and measure nothing) and it never writes an expectation back. `--control` perturbs every published expectation AND every pinned constant and requires each to be reported, so the green is falsifiable. Exit 0 = agreed, 1 = disagreed (a different answer, printed `DISAGREE:`, or the authority RAISED where this file records an answer, printed `RAISED:`), 2 = could not measure. SHAPE NOTE: `terminalsForBoard` / `terminalNamesForBoardId` answer an ordered list on the mirror and a frozenset on the authority; the runner compares them as SETS, because order is not part of this rule.
not_checked_by_this_repo: NOTHING HERE REDS WHEN THE COORDINATION FRAMEWORK CHANGES ITS OWN PYTHON. The bridge's suite holds the MIRROR against this file; the far-end half is `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py`, which is deliberately NOT in this repo's CI, because CI has no copy of the authority (it is a plugin the bridge does not vendor). A green bridge suite says the mirror still answers what this file publishes — never that the authority still does.

Both arms are MEMBER-GRANULAR. A branch, a guard or an inline literal edited INSIDE an existing public method is outside both: the reverse arm counts member names, and the vector arm only sees a change that moves one of the published answers.

MALFORMED CONFIG IS OUTSIDE THE PARITY CLAIM, and `known_divergences` pins where. The mirror type-guards every value it reads out of `coordination.config.json` (`is_array`, `is_string`, non-empty) and the authority does not. That is ONE shape with four measured instances, not four defects, and the mirror's behaviour is the deliberate one — it reads a file it does not own, over a path a lower-trust principal can influence. The divergent answers are inert downstream: a per-character or empty-string 'terminal' matches no column on either side.

THREE MALFORMED-CONFIG SHAPES MAKE THE AUTHORITY RAISE RATHER THAN ANSWER, so they have no value to pin and are named here instead (measured 2026-09-24 against agent-board-framework coord plugin 0.55.0, templates/kanban/examples): a `board_id` that is a non-numeric string other than `REPLACE_ME` on an entry that HAS terminals, and `"8.5"`, both raise `ValueError` from `int()`; a `kanban.boards[]` member that is not an object raises `AttributeError`. The mirror skips all three and answers []. An operator hand-editing that file gets a crashed reconcile and a quiet bridge.

`load()` and `issuePopulationsForBoardId()` carry NO parity vectors, for DIFFERENT reasons. `load()` is bridge-local and has no shared observable (`mirror_local`). `issuePopulationsForBoardId()` is NOT: it mirrors the authority's `issue_population` rule, which the far end can observe, and the runner does not drive it — so it is an UNCHECKED COPY, and `mirrored_but_not_driven` names the authority sites and the drift that goes undetected at both ends. It also carries a known divergence that cannot be pinned as a value pair: the authority REFUSES an unrecognised `issue_population` (`raise SystemExit` naming the key, in `reconcile_simple_board`) where this mirror resolves anything that is not literally 'all' to 'prefixed'.

The measurement is against ONE version of the authority (`last_measured.authority_ref`). An install running a different coord version is UNMEASURED, not agreed — re-run the runner against your own copy.

last_measured.authority_blob: sha256:f85539708a76baf2bab3cb730ba3e3b3204849faa72295605ae56e7b5094dc68 (kanban_common.py), sha256:3050448adacb117f7555d2b179ee66c0bce80301688a0eab1fbfc08bf42647c7 (_kanban_read.py, which owns the `load_config` the join reads through), sha256:2b2283cc782b38ee0d94c6d711c06976bfb5f44d97e742018c9890c436cbfdfa (kanban-inbox-check.py), sha256:e4f88a492818eb2433a3f7b1b5b1543a6632215ceee5ef25cfa17dd3516f3d3a (kanban-issues-sync.py, loaded by the same run) — copied from the runner's own `executed:` lines, not typed
last_measured.method: `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py --corpus docs/coord-terminals-parity-corpus.json` executed every vector and every known divergence below against the authority named above — with the `coord` package bound to that directory, so `_terminal_columns_by_board` reached the `kanban_common` named here. ⚠ RE-TAKEN, and why: the FIRST measurement did not. The scripts' `from coord.kanban_common import …` resolved on `sys.path` to an installed copy with different bytes, so the `terminalNamesForBoardId` half ran against an authority this block did not name; it agreed only because `terminals_for_board`'s body happened to be identical in both copies (PR #786 review r1). It then held `DEFAULT_TERMINAL` against `terminals_for_board`'s own `default_terminal` parameter default AND against `kanban-inbox-check`'s `DONE_COLUMN` (one mirror constant, two authority sites — if those two ever disagree the mirror cannot match both, and the runner says so). The same invocation with `--control` was run and reported EVERY perturbed expectation and EVERY perturbed pinned constant. Whoever adds, changes or DELETES a vector re-takes this measurement over the WHOLE corpus and rewrites `vectors_digest`; the bridge's own suite reds until they do.
last_measured.result: AGREED, AND THE DISAGREEMENTS ARE NAMED RATHER THAN ABSENT. Every one of the 26 vectors and all 4 known divergences above was EXECUTED against the authority named in `authority_ref`, and `DEFAULT_TERMINAL` was read off `terminals_for_board`'s own signature and off `kanban-inbox-check.DONE_COLUMN`; all agreed. The run is falsifiable: the same command with `--control` perturbed every expectation and the pinned constant, and reported every one. ⚠ THIS IS A DATED OBSERVATION OF ONE AUTHORITY VERSION, NOT A STANDING PROPERTY — nothing in the bridge's CI re-takes it, because CI has no copy of the authority.

not_mirrored.done_column= / terminal_columns= kwargs: `terminals_for_board` folds two DEPRECATED adapter kwargs for un-migrated callers. Its own docstring is explicit that the READ-site sees none of them ('only terminals present in CONFIG are visible to the read-site'), and this mirror is a read-site, so they are deliberately not mirrored. Vector `terminalsForBoard#9` pins that a `done_column` KEY in the config (as opposed to the kwarg) is inert on both ends.
not_mirrored.lifecycle_rank_for_board and the rest of: Out of scope. The bridge mirrors the terminal rule only; nothing here claims anything about the authority's other primitives.

mirror_local.load: The bridge's own guarded reader for `coordination.config.json` (card#9121's `UntrustedPathContents`). The authority resolves $COORD_CONFIG through `kanban_common.load_config()`, whose contract — throw vs None, size cap, symlink handling — is a property of the PROCESS doing the reading and not of the terminal rule. There is no shared observable, and publishing a 'parity' vector for one would dress a local expectation up as a cross-repo agreement. `CoordConfigTerminalsTest` pins its local behaviour.

mirrored_but_not_driven.issuePopulationsForBoardId: Mirrors the coordination framework's `kanban.boards[].issue_population` rule, and the far end CAN observe that rule — it is NOT bridge-local, which is why this member is not in `mirror_local`. The authority reads it at these sites (coord 0.55.0, `last_measured.authority_ref`): `kanban_common.reconcile_simple_board` (`_population = (bc.get("issue_population") or "prefixed")`, which raises `SystemExit` naming the key on any value other than `prefixed` or `all`, and gates the by-ref reconcile leg on `all`), and `kanban-issues-sync.main` (`_coord_all = (board_config("issues").get("issue_population") or "prefixed") == "all"`, which gates the sync-side by-ref stamp and validates nothing). The authority's own `test_byref_reconcile_leg.py` observes the first site by stubbing the board client. `bin/coord-mirror-parity.py` does NOT drive either site — it has no adapter for this member, so no vector is published for it and nothing here claims the two ends agree. THE DRIFT THIS LEAVES UNDETECTED AT BOTH ENDS: the authority accepting a new value, changing its default, changing the key it reads, or changing how it selects the board entry (it selects by board KEY — `board_config("issues")` and the key `reconcile_simple_board` is called with — where this mirror joins by `board_id`) would move `bridge:check`'s bridge-vs-reconcile `issue_population` compare (`WritebackMappingConfigCheck`) to a wrong answer, and neither this repo's suite nor the runner would red. One divergence is KNOWN and not pinned, because one side has no value to pin: the reconcile REFUSES an unrecognised value where this mirror resolves anything that is not literally `all` to `prefixed`. `CoordConfigTerminalsTest` pins the mirror's local behaviour only.

terminalsForBoard.why: A STRING where the schema says list. Python's `set("Done")` splits it into characters; the mirror's `is_array` guard answers no terminals. ONE SHAPE with the three below: the mirror type-guards an untrusted config file and the authority does not. Inert downstream — no column is named 'D'.
An EMPTY-STRING member. The authority keeps it; the mirror's `$name !== ''` drops it. Same shape. Inert downstream — no column is named ''.
A NON-STRING member. The authority keeps the integer; the mirror's `is_string` drops it. Same shape. Inert downstream — no column is named 5.

`user_lanes` as a non-empty STRING. Python tests truthiness and falls back to the default terminal; the mirror requires a non-empty ARRAY. Same shape, and the ONE instance whose divergent answer is NOT inert — the authority concludes 'Done' is terminal on that board and the mirror concludes nothing is, so `bridge:check` would report agreement it does not have. It takes a hand-edited config to reach.

terminalsForBoard.note: the ordinary shape: one explicit terminal.
several explicit terminals, returned VERBATIM in the vocabulary config spells them.
the DUAL-VOCABULARY case the framework's own docs require: a terminal listed by display name AND stage external_id. Neither end resolves or filters either spelling.
THE LANE-MODEL FALLBACK, and the one the DL-200 spec text originally missed: a board declaring `user_lanes` and NO `terminal_columns` resolves the `default_terminal`, not nothing.
a board with neither explicit terminals nor `user_lanes` has NO terminals — it never concludes anything. NEGATIVE.
an EMPTY explicit list still reaches the lane-model fallback: the authority's condition is `if not terminals`, not `if 'terminal_columns' not in cfg`.
explicit terminals SUPPRESS the fallback rather than unioning with it — 'Done' appears once, not twice.
an EMPTY `user_lanes` is not the lane model. NEGATIVE, and the pair to #5: `[]` is falsy in Python and `!== []` in the mirror, which is why both answer nothing.
duplicates collapse — a set on the authority, a keyed array on the mirror.
a `done_column` KEY in the config is NOT read by either end: it is a deprecated adapter KWARG, and this is a read-site. NEGATIVE, and the one that pins `not_mirrored`.
the same, beside a real terminal: 'Shipped' is not folded in.

an explicit NULL `terminal_columns` falls through to the lane model on both ends — the authority's `or ()` and the mirror's `is_array` agree here, which is what makes the string case in `known_divergences` a shape rather than an accident.
a FALSY non-array `user_lanes`: both ends answer nothing. NEGATIVE, and the control for the `user_lanes: "stage-next"` divergence — it shows the two ends part on truthiness-vs-type, not on the key.

terminalNamesForBoardId.note: the ordinary shape: one board entry, joined by board ID.
a board id no entry carries resolves NOTHING. NEGATIVE — and the reason the mirror must not read [] as 'no terminals declared anywhere'.
TWO entries sharing one physical board id (a `prs` + `product-tasks` pair) UNION their terminals rather than the last winning.
a NUMERIC STRING board id joins — real configs carry "8" where the framework's own vectors use 8.
the `REPLACE_ME` placeholder is INERT on both ends. NEGATIVE.
the lane-model fallback reaches the by-id read too — this is the canonical `issues` board's real shape.
an entry that declares no terminals contributes none, and the board resolves to nothing. NEGATIVE.
a NULL board id is skipped by both ends — the authority by its explicit sentinel list, the mirror by `is_numeric`. NEGATIVE.
several boards, asking for the SECOND: the join key is the board id and nothing leaks between entries.
a FLOAT board id joins on both ends. It also exercises the digest's float typing — `8` and `8.0` are different inputs and a JSON reformat must not silently retype this vector.
